domain_label: Compact Code and Library Representation (LLM Engineering subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is token-efficient code/library representation for LLM code generation, finer than a whole-codegen KB
the encode->generate->decode cycle is the organizing metaphor: repr is an intermediate compressed form
primary use case is retrieval-augmented code generation where compact repr tokens replace verbatim source in context
exclusions: full program synthesis beyond API-level generation
model pre-training data curation for code
code review and static analysis beyond type grounding
package manager and dependency resolution infrastructure

competency_questions.question: What elements are included vs excluded from compact code/library representation and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPR_SCHEMA and NATURALNESS define inclusion/exclusion policy

competency_questions.question: How is the repr index kept consistent as libraries release new versions?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VERSION_MGMT INCREMENTAL_UPDATE REPR_VERSIONING define version lifecycle

competency_questions.question: How are API signatures and docstrings compressed while preserving semantic completeness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIG_COMPRESS DOCSTR_DISTILL USAGE_EX define compression approach

competency_questions.question: How is type information encoded in the compact repr to enable type-directed generation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TYPE_AWARE and DEP_GRAPH define type and dependency encoding

competency_questions.question: How are token budget tradeoffs managed across signature, type, docstring, and example components?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TOKEN_BUDGET defines allocation; conflict edges show resolution

competency_questions.question: How is the encoding pipeline designed to produce a consistent reproducible repr index?
How is a natural language or code query encoded to retrieve relevant API repr entries?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETRIEVAL_INDEX and QUERY_ENCODE define retrieval path

competency_questions.question: How is compact repr expanded back to usable code in the decode stage?
How is repr injected into the LLM generation prompt and how does fine-tuning reduce injection overhead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTEXT_INJECT and FINETUNE_REPR define generation integration

competency_questions.question: How is the overall encode->generate->decode cycle evaluated for quality and correctness?
How are hallucinations detected and coverage gaps managed in the repr-grounded system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HALLUC_GUARD and COVERAGE_GAP define QA approach

competency_questions.question: How are retrieval and injection latency and cost managed within SLA constraints?

glossary.definition: token-efficient intermediate encoding of a library API entry: signatures compressed types distilled docstrings minimal examples; replaces verbatim source in LLM context
three-stage pipeline: encode library source to compact repr generate code using repr-augmented LLM decode repr tokens back to executable idiomatic code
lossless or near-lossless reduction of API function/class signatures to minimal token form preserving type and call information
maximum number of tokens allocated for repr of a library or per-function entry within an LLM context window
RAG pattern applied to code: retrieve relevant API repr entries given a user query inject into LLM prompt to guide correct API usage
serialized database of encoded library repr entries indexed for fast retrieval by API name type or semantic query
repr that encodes type annotations (generics protocols nullable) such that the generator can produce type-safe code without runtime type checker
empirical property of code that it follows repetitive predictable patterns similar to natural language (Allamanis et al. 2018) enabling entropy-guided compression
verification that generated API calls have corresponding entries in the repr index flagging ungrounded calls as potential hallucinations

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for compact code/library representation work units; informed by Allamanis et al. 2018 naturalness survey and Manning Raghavan Schutze IR principles
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Allamanis et al. 2018 A Survey of ML for Big Code and Naturalness; Manning Raghavan Schutze Introduction to Information Retrieval

nodes.definition: Define the canonical schema for compact code/library representation: which elements to encode (signatures, docstrings, type annotations, usage examples, dependency graph edges) and what to elide (implementation bodies, comments, redundant boilerplate).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: library schema or type system changes materially

pros.claim: Single authoritative schema prevents representation drift across encode-generate-decode cycle
pros.example: repr schema used by both indexer and generator ensures round-trip fidelity

cons.claim: Over-elision of context causes ambiguous reconstruction and hallucinated implementations
cons.example: stripping all docstrings causes model to invent wrong parameter semantics

failure_modes: schema over-elision causing reconstruction ambiguity
schema bloat exceeding token budget
acceptance_tests: schema serializes a held-out set of functions and round-trips through decode with less than 5 percent semantic error
every required field present in 100 percent of encoded units
revisit_triggers: library API surface expands by more than 20 new public symbols
type system changes such as new generic syntax

nodes.definition: Quantify and manage the token budget consumed by encoded library representations; balance compression ratio vs semantic completeness to fit within LLM context windows without losing critical API detail.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window constraints or library size changes

pros.claim: Explicit budget prevents context overflow that silently truncates critical API entries
pros.example: fitting 200 library signatures into 4096 tokens via field elision

cons.claim: Aggressive compression loses type nuance needed for correct code generation
cons.example: truncating return types causes model to assume wrong output shape

failure_modes: token budget exceeded silently truncating repr
over-compression losing semantic discriminators
acceptance_tests: encoded repr for benchmark library fits target context window at 90 percent or more signature coverage
compression ratio documented and reproducible
revisit_triggers: LLM context window size changes
library grows beyond token budget allocation

nodes.definition: Compress API signatures (function/class/method names, parameter types, return types, overloads) into maximally token-efficient notation while preserving all information needed to call the API correctly.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: API surface or type system substantially revised

pros.claim: Overload deduplication via delta encoding reduces token cost 40-60 percent for polymorphic APIs
pros.example: numpy.array overloads collapsed to single parametric form

cons.claim: Lossy signature compression causes model to generate wrong argument types
cons.example: removing Optional annotation causes model to omit None-handling

failure_modes: stripping Optional/Union annotations causing type errors
overload collapse losing dispatch information
acceptance_tests: compressed signature can be decoded back to original with zero type errors on held-out set
compression ratio 3x or more on overloaded APIs
revisit_triggers: new Python type syntax via PEP updates
overload explosion in updated library

nodes.definition: Encode type information (generics, ADTs, protocols, structural types) in representation such that the LLM can perform type-directed generation and avoid type errors without access to the full type checker.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: type system constructs added to language or library

pros.claim: Type-aware repr enables LLM to generate type-safe code without external checker at generation time
pros.example: encoding Tensor shape annotation reduces shape-mismatch errors

cons.claim: Complex generic types explode token cost and risk confusing the model
cons.example: deeply nested TypeVar constraints exceed model effective attention span

failure_modes: over-specifying generics consuming excessive tokens
stripping nullability causing None errors
acceptance_tests: type-directed generation benchmark: less than 10 percent type errors on held-out API call tasks
all Optional/Union/Protocol types encoded in standard normalized form
revisit_triggers: language type system adds new constructs such as TypeVarTuple or ParamSpec
library adopts Protocol-heavy design

nodes.definition: Distill verbose docstrings into minimal semantic-preserving summaries: retain parameter semantics, return value semantics, raised exceptions, and key behavioral constraints; discard examples, formatting, and redundant prose.

excluded: changelog and version notes in docstrings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: docstring style or coverage changes in target library

pros.claim: Distilled docstrings reduce per-function token cost 5-10x while retaining semantic correctness
pros.example: keras.fit docstring: 800 tokens to 80 tokens with param/return/exception preserved

cons.claim: Distillation can lose edge-case behavioral constraints causing incorrect API usage
cons.example: stripping raises ValueError if axis out of bounds causes uncaught exceptions

failure_modes: over-distillation losing exception or constraint information
under-distillation wasting token budget
acceptance_tests: distillation recall: 95 percent or more of behavioral constraints preserved on evaluation set
token reduction 5x or more vs raw docstring on benchmark libraries
revisit_triggers: documentation style overhaul in target libraries
new semantic content types added to docstrings

nodes.definition: Leverage the naturalness hypothesis (Allamanis et al. 2018) that code is repetitive and predictable like natural language; use n-gram/bimodal statistics to guide what to compress (high-entropy unique tokens) vs retain (low-entropy idiomatic patterns).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: code naturalness distribution changes in target domain

pros.claim: High-entropy unique identifiers need repr; low-entropy idiomatic patterns can be abbreviated or omitted
pros.example: for i in range(len(x)) is idiomatic and can be represented by opaque idiom-id

cons.claim: Naturalness statistics shift across domains; library utility code less natural than application code
cons.example: numpy internal C-binding wrappers do not follow Python naturalness distribution

failure_modes: naturalness stats from wrong domain degrading elision policy
treating domain-specific APIs as idiomatic when they are unique
acceptance_tests: elision policy validated: naturalness-guided repr recovers 90 percent or more of token reduction with less than 5 percent semantic loss vs full encoding
entropy scores computed on representative corpus before use
revisit_triggers: new programming paradigms shift naturalness distribution
switch to new language or library ecosystem

nodes.definition: Select and encode minimal but representative usage examples in the repr to guide the LLM toward correct API usage patterns; balance example token cost against generation fidelity improvement.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: API usage patterns or token budget constraints change

pros.claim: One minimal usage example per API reduces model hallucination of incorrect argument order
pros.example: example df.merge(right, on=key) prevents positional arg confusion

cons.claim: Too many examples crowd out signature information in limited token budget
cons.example: 3 examples per function leaves no room for type information

failure_modes: example token budget crowding out type/signature information
unrepresentative examples teaching wrong usage patterns
acceptance_tests: usage example repr improves generation accuracy 10 percent or more over no-example baseline on held-out tasks
example budget capped at configurable per-function token limit
revisit_triggers: API usage patterns shift with new idioms
token budget constraints tighten

nodes.definition: Encode inter-API dependency relationships (calls, inherits, uses, returns) as a compact graph in the repr index so the generator can navigate transitive dependencies and avoid broken import chains.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: library refactoring changes dependency structure

pros.claim: Encoding 1-hop dependency graph enables model to generate correct import chains without hallucinating missing imports
pros.example: knowing torch.nn.Module requires import torch.nn prevents import Module hallucination

cons.claim: Deep transitive dependency encoding explodes repr size and hits token budget
cons.example: encoding 10-hop chain for a utility function wastes context

failure_modes: transitive dep explosion exceeding token budget
stale dep graph after library refactor
acceptance_tests: dep graph round-trip: all 1-hop dependencies correctly recovered from repr on benchmark
dep encoding size bounded to 10 percent or less of total repr token budget
revisit_triggers: library major refactor changes call graph structure
new dependency types added

nodes.definition: Design and implement the end-to-end pipeline that ingests library source/stubs, applies signature compression, type encoding, docstring distillation, and produces a token-counted repr index ready for retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: upstream library or pipeline toolchain changes

pros.claim: Automated pipeline ensures reproducible index updates when libraries release new versions
pros.example: CI-triggered re-encoding after pip install upgrade

cons.claim: Pipeline bugs silently corrupt repr index causing downstream hallucinations
cons.example: wrong charset handling strips Unicode type names

failure_modes: silent corruption of repr index
incremental update missing changed symbols
acceptance_tests: pipeline is idempotent: re-running on same input produces identical index
full re-encode of top-50 Python libraries completes in less than 2 hours
revisit_triggers: library release cadence increases
pipeline input format changes

nodes.definition: Manage multiple concurrent library versions in the repr index; encode version metadata alongside signatures to enable version-conditional generation and prevent cross-version API confusion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: major library version release or API deprecation

pros.claim: Version tagging prevents model from generating API calls valid only in library v2 for a v1 user
pros.example: torch.compile tagged as 2.0 or later prevents generation for PyTorch 1.x users

cons.claim: Multi-version index multiplies index size and retrieval complexity
cons.example: maintaining numpy 1.x and 2.x repr doubles index footprint

failure_modes: cross-version API confusion
index size explosion from too many versions
acceptance_tests: version-conditional generation test: correct version API used for 95 percent or more of versioned benchmark tasks
index size bounded by retaining only N most recent semver-major versions
revisit_triggers: major library version bump with breaking API changes
LTS version support policy changes

nodes.definition: Build a retrieval index over the encoded library repr corpus enabling fast lookup of relevant API signatures given a natural language or code query; supports both lexical (BM25) and semantic (embedding) retrieval.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: retrieval benchmark results or repr schema changes

pros.claim: Hybrid retrieval combining BM25 on token-compressed signatures with dense embeddings maximizes recall for both exact-name and paraphrase queries
pros.example: BM25 catches pandas.DataFrame.merge; dense catches join two tables

cons.claim: Embedding drift if repr schema changes without re-indexing degrades retrieval quality
cons.example: token-level changes to repr format shift embedding space

failure_modes: embedding drift after repr schema change
BM25 misses paraphrase queries
acceptance_tests: retrieval recall@10 90 percent or more on held-out query set
index re-build triggered automatically on repr schema version change
revisit_triggers: repr schema version change
new embedding model adopted

nodes.definition: Transform a natural language or partial code query into a representation compatible with the repr retrieval index; includes intent classification, keyword extraction, and embedding projection aligned to the repr index space.
inputs: natural language or partial code query

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: query vocabulary or repr notation changes

pros.claim: Intent-aware query encoding distinguishes how-to-use queries from what-signature queries
pros.example: classifying as signature-query routes to BM25 on compressed sigs

cons.claim: Domain shift between NL query and compressed repr notation degrades retrieval
cons.example: users say merge dataframes but repr encodes join in compressed form

failure_modes: vocabulary mismatch between NL query and compressed repr notation
ambiguous code context causing wrong intent class
acceptance_tests: query encoding round-trip: encoded query retrieves correct API in top-3 for 85 percent or more of benchmark cases
intent classifier accuracy 88 percent or more on held-out query sample
revisit_triggers: repr schema token notation changes
new query intent types observed

nodes.definition: Expand a retrieved compact repr back to full usable code: reconstruct imports, instantiate parameter defaults, add boilerplate, and emit idiomatic usage patterns - the decode stage of the encode->generate->decode cycle.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: library import structure or repr schema changes

pros.claim: Expand-decode stage converts compressed repr tokens back to executable code the user can copy-paste
pros.example: from compressed np.arr(shape,dtype) expand to import numpy as np; np.array(shape, dtype=dtype)

cons.claim: Incomplete expansion leaves placeholder tokens the user must manually replace reducing trust
cons.example: unexpanded T generic type left in generated code

failure_modes: unexpanded placeholder tokens in output
wrong import path reconstruction for submodule APIs
acceptance_tests: expand-decode produces syntactically valid Python for 95 percent or more of retrieved API repr on benchmark
all import statements correct and resolvable on benchmark library set
revisit_triggers: library import structure changes such as submodule reorganization
repr schema changes affecting decode mapping

nodes.definition: Design the prompt template and injection strategy for inserting retrieved repr tokens into the LLM generation prompt: placement, formatting, length management, and context priority ordering.

excluded: system prompt design outside repr injection

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: context window or prompt injection policy changes

pros.claim: Structured repr injection with role markers improves model attention to injected context vs prompt prose
pros.example: explicit section headers increase API usage accuracy by reducing attention diffusion

cons.claim: Exceeding context window with repr tokens truncates user task description silently
cons.example: retrieving 20 API entries for a simple task crowds out the user code context

failure_modes: repr injection crowding out task context
model ignoring injected repr due to positional bias
acceptance_tests: context injection benchmark: 80 percent or more of generated code uses at least one injected API correctly
injected repr never truncates user task description
revisit_triggers: model context window changes
repr schema notation changes that break model parsing of injection markers

nodes.definition: Evaluate representation quality via round-trip fidelity (encode->generate->decode correctness), retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR), and generation quality (exact match, type correctness, execution correctness on benchmarks).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark results or evaluation methodology changes

pros.claim: Multi-axis evaluation (retrieval + generation + execution) catches failures that single-axis eval misses
pros.example: retrieval recall can be high while generation has systematic type errors

cons.claim: Pass@k with LLM judge risks Goodhart: model optimizes repr for judge not correctness
cons.example: repr tuned to match judge descriptions fails execution tests

failure_modes: Goodharting on judge-based eval instead of execution
benchmark contamination if library APIs overlap training data
acceptance_tests: eval pipeline runs in CI on every repr schema change
execution correctness 70 percent or more pass@1 on HumanEval-style API tasks
revisit_triggers: benchmark contamination detected
evaluation metric changes

nodes.definition: Implement repr-grounded hallucination detection: verify generated API calls against the repr index at generation time or post-generation, flagging calls with no matching repr entry as potential hallucinations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repr index coverage or hallucination rate changes

pros.claim: Membership-test against repr index catches fabricated API names before code reaches user
pros.example: pd.DataFrame.pivot_wide() not in repr index flags as likely hallucination

cons.claim: Repr index coverage gaps cause false positives: valid rare APIs flagged as hallucinations
cons.example: private or newly-added APIs not yet in index trigger false flags

failure_modes: repr index coverage gaps causing false hallucination flags
grounding check latency adding unacceptable overhead
acceptance_tests: hallucination detection precision 90 percent or more on benchmark of known-hallucinated API calls
false positive rate less than 10 percent on valid-but-rare API calls
revisit_triggers: repr index coverage grows beyond grounding check capacity
latency budget for grounding check changes

nodes.definition: Fine-tune the LLM to natively understand and generate from the compact repr notation, improving generation fidelity and reducing context needed for in-context teaching of the notation.

included: SFT data construction from repr index

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repr schema or base model changes requiring re-fine-tuning

pros.claim: Fine-tuning on repr format reduces in-context teaching tokens needed per query freeing context for more API entries
pros.example: repr-native model uses zero format-explanation tokens vs 300 for in-context-only approach

cons.claim: SFT on narrow repr format risks catastrophic forgetting of general coding capability
cons.example: repr-fine-tuned model degrades on non-API coding tasks

failure_modes: catastrophic forgetting of general coding capability
SFT data contamination with benchmark tasks
acceptance_tests: repr-fine-tuned model passes general coding benchmark within 5 percent of base model
repr-native generation accuracy 10 percent or more above in-context-only baseline
revisit_triggers: repr schema changes requiring SFT re-run
base model updated requiring re-fine-tuning

nodes.definition: Model and manage end-to-end latency and cost of the encode->retrieve->inject->generate->decode pipeline; identify bottlenecks (retrieval latency, repr injection token cost, fine-tuning amortization) and enforce SLAs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: latency SLA or model token cost changes

pros.claim: Profiling identifies retrieval as dominant latency: caching top-k repr for frequent APIs reduces p99 latency 60 percent
pros.example: LRU cache over repr index hits reduces retrieval from 200ms to 10ms

cons.claim: Optimizing for latency by reducing retrieval depth degrades recall and hallucination rate
cons.example: top-1 retrieval instead of top-10 saves 50ms but misses correct API 30 percent of time

failure_modes: latency-quality tradeoff optimized at wrong operating point
cost model underestimating token injection overhead
acceptance_tests: end-to-end pipeline latency measured and documented
SLA met for 99 percent or more of requests in load test
revisit_triggers: model updated changing token cost
SLA requirements tighten

nodes.definition: Detect and manage gaps in repr coverage (APIs present in user code but absent from repr index); implement graceful fallback (retrieval from raw docs, web search, or refusal) and coverage expansion workflow.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: coverage gap rate or user query distribution changes

pros.claim: Coverage gap reporting drives prioritized index expansion: top-10 missing APIs in user queries added first
pros.example: usage-log-driven coverage expansion reduces top-10 gap rate 80 percent in first sprint

cons.claim: Silent coverage gaps cause hallucination without user awareness; fallback must be explicit
cons.example: model generates fabricated API when gap is silent vs explicit uncertainty signal

failure_modes: silent coverage gaps causing hallucination without user warning
coverage expansion bottlenecked by pipeline throughput
acceptance_tests: coverage gap detection rate 95 percent or more: known-missing APIs flagged not silently hallucinated
fallback policy triggers explicit uncertainty signal for all gap cases
revisit_triggers: user query distribution shifts exposing new gap areas
library adds major new subsystem

nodes.definition: Update the repr index incrementally when libraries release new versions: detect changed/added/removed symbols, re-encode only affected entries, and propagate dependency graph changes without full re-index.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: library release cadence or repr schema version changes

pros.claim: Incremental update reduces re-encode time from hours to minutes for typical patch releases
pros.example: only 5 percent of numpy symbols change per minor release; incremental costs 5 percent of full re-index time

cons.claim: Incremental logic bugs leave stale repr entries for removed APIs causing hallucination
cons.example: deleted function still in repr index after library removes it

failure_modes: stale repr entries for removed APIs
dep graph inconsistency after structural change
acceptance_tests: incremental update produces identical index to full re-index on benchmark library patch release
stale entry detection test: removed APIs not present in updated index
revisit_triggers: library reorganization requiring structural re-index
repr schema version bump requiring full re-encode

nodes.definition: Align repr notation and identifier namespaces across multiple libraries to enable the model to generate code combining APIs from different libraries without namespace collisions or import confusion.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new library added or cross-library namespace collision detected

pros.claim: Cross-library alignment prevents torch Tensor vs tensorflow Tensor collision in generated imports
pros.example: explicit namespace prefixes in repr: torch::Tensor vs tf::Tensor

cons.claim: Alignment overhead adds encoding complexity and risks over-normalizing library-specific idioms
cons.example: forcing pandas and polars into same repr schema loses polars lazy evaluation distinction

failure_modes: namespace collision in multi-library generation
over-normalization losing library-specific semantics
acceptance_tests: cross-library generation test: correct import namespace used for 95 percent or more of multi-library API calls
namespace collision rate less than 0.01 in benchmark multi-library tasks
revisit_triggers: new library added to index
library API breaking change affects cross-library alignment

nodes.definition: Version the repr schema itself and manage migrations: track schema version in each repr entry, migrate old entries to new schema on upgrade, and maintain backward compatibility for fine-tuned models trained on old schema.

excluded: library version management handled in VERSION_MGMT

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repr schema major version change or fine-tuned model retrain

pros.claim: Schema versioning prevents silent incompatibility between repr index built on v1 schema and model fine-tuned on v2 schema
pros.example: version mismatch error caught at load time rather than silent generation degradation

cons.claim: Migration scripts add engineering overhead and risk introducing repr corruption
cons.example: migration bug corrupts all signature entries for abstract base classes

failure_modes: migration script corrupting repr entries
fine-tuned model incompatible with migrated schema
acceptance_tests: schema migration produces valid repr entries verified by schema validator on 100 percent of migrated entries
fine-tuned model compatibility tested before schema migration deployed
revisit_triggers: repr schema major revision
fine-tuned model retrained on new schema

edges.resolution_rule: Resolve by fixing type_aware as inner layer: compress signatures first then annotate types in normalized compressed form; do not further compress type tokens below minimum resolution
Resolve by allocating token budget: docstring distill gets 60 percent of per-function budget usage examples get 40 percent; enforced by TOKEN_BUDGET allocation table
Resolve by separating concerns: in-context injection is the runtime path; fine-tuning is an offline path to reduce injection token overhead; they are complementary not exclusive
Resolve by schema version gating: fine-tuning runs are tagged with schema version; model retrain is triggered when schema major version changes not for minor/patch updates

Resolve by caching and tiered retrieval: implement LRU cache for top-k frequent repr queries; accept higher latency for rare queries where cache misses; set explicit latency budget before recall tradeoff
Resolve by repr length budgeting enforced at injection time: hard cap on repr tokens injected per request; prioritize by retrieval score
Resolve by shared budget allocation table owned by TOKEN_BUDGET node; CONTEXT_INJECT defers to it for per-request repr token limits

conflict_axes.name: compression_vs_semantic_completeness
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive token compression reduces context overhead but risks losing type nuance exception semantics and behavioral constraints needed for correct code generation
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: set minimum semantic completeness requirements first (types exceptions constraints) then compress remaining prose to budget

conflict_axes.name: retrieval_depth_vs_latency
conflict_axes.description: Deeper retrieval (higher top-k) improves recall and reduces hallucination but increases retrieval latency and token injection cost
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: profile latency budget first; cache top-k for frequent queries; accept shallow retrieval only when p99 latency would breach SLA

conflict_axes.name: fine_tuning_vs_in_context_repr
conflict_axes.description: Fine-tuning the model on repr format reduces per-query context overhead but adds training cost risks catastrophic forgetting and requires re-training on repr schema changes
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use in-context injection as default; add fine-tuning only when token injection overhead consistently exceeds 20 percent of context window

conflict_axes.name: index_coverage_vs_index_size
conflict_axes.description: Maximizing repr index coverage reduces hallucinations but increases index size retrieval latency and encoding pipeline cost
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: prioritize coverage by query frequency; encode top-N most-queried APIs first; set index size budget

conflict_axes.name: type_detail_vs_token_cost
conflict_axes.description: Encoding rich generic and protocol type information improves type-directed generation but consumes large token budget for complex type signatures
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: always encode nullability and top-level generics; elide deeply nested TypeVar constraints beyond 2 levels

conflict_axes.name: multi_version_repr_vs_index_complexity
conflict_axes.description: Supporting multiple library versions in repr index prevents cross-version API confusion but multiplies index size and retrieval complexity
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: retain N most recent semver-major versions; deprecate older entries; version-tag all entries for conditional retrieval

conflict_axes.name: usage_examples_vs_signature_space
conflict_axes.description: Including usage examples in repr improves generation fidelity but consumes token budget that could be used for additional API signatures
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: allocate fixed per-function example budget; include example only for APIs with known high misuse rate

conflict_axes.name: hallucination_guard_recall_vs_precision
conflict_axes.description: Strict repr grounding catches more hallucinations but increases false positive rate for valid rare APIs not yet in index
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: set confidence threshold based on index coverage rate; use soft flag (uncertainty) not hard rejection for borderline cases

conflict_axes.name: naturalness_guided_vs_uniform_compression
conflict_axes.description: Naturalness-guided elision tailors compression to code statistics but adds complexity and may fail for domain-specific code that is less natural
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use naturalness statistics as soft prior for compression; override with fixed minimum information rules for low-naturalness library internals

conflict_axes.name: cross_library_alignment_vs_per_library_fidelity
conflict_axes.description: Aligning repr notation across libraries enables multi-library generation but risks losing library-specific idioms and semantic distinctions
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: enforce shared structural schema; allow library-specific notation extensions as tagged fields; resolve collisions with explicit namespace prefixes

edge_cases.description: Library API surface exceeds token budget for any single context window
edge_cases.trigger: encoding top-level module with more than 1000 public symbols
edge_cases.risk: repr truncation silently drops critical APIs
edge_cases.mitigation: hierarchical repr: encode module-level summaries retrieve sub-module repr on demand

edge_cases.description: Library removes a public API between repr index build and user query
edge_cases.trigger: library deprecation and removal between index builds
edge_cases.risk: hallucination guard fails to catch removed API usage
edge_cases.mitigation: incremental update triggered on library release; version-conditional retrieval warns on deprecated API

edge_cases.description: User query uses natural language that has no lexical overlap with compressed repr notation
edge_cases.trigger: user says combine dataframes but repr uses compressed join form
edge_cases.risk: BM25 retrieval fails; semantic retrieval required
edge_cases.mitigation: hybrid retrieval mandatory; query encoder must bridge NL-repr vocabulary gap

edge_cases.description: Repr schema major version change breaks fine-tuned model compatibility
edge_cases.trigger: repr schema v2 changes compressed notation for generic types
edge_cases.risk: model fine-tuned on v1 schema generates malformed code using v2 repr
edge_cases.mitigation: schema version gating: model retraining triggered before schema version deployed to index

edge_cases.description: Cross-library namespace collision in generated imports
edge_cases.trigger: both pytorch and tensorflow define Tensor; repr uses same unqualified token
edge_cases.risk: generated import uses wrong framework Tensor in multi-library task
edge_cases.mitigation: cross-library alignment enforces namespace prefixes in repr; CROSS_LIB node mandatory before multi-library tasks

edge_cases.description: Deeply recursive generic type annotation explodes repr token count
edge_cases.trigger: Callable with nested Dict List Tuple types in repr
edge_cases.risk: single type annotation consumes entire per-function token budget
edge_cases.mitigation: type depth limit: encode generics to max 2 levels; represent deeper types as opaque type alias with expansion on demand

edge_cases.description: Repr index built on stubs diverges from runtime behavior
edge_cases.trigger: type stub incorrectly documents return type vs actual runtime
edge_cases.risk: model generates type-correct but semantically wrong code
edge_cases.mitigation: supplement stub-based repr with runtime-validated usage examples; flag stub-only entries with lower confidence

edge_cases.description: High query volume saturates retrieval index cache degrading latency
edge_cases.trigger: burst query traffic for same library
edge_cases.risk: p99 latency breaches SLA; repr injection stalled
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-warm cache for top-N libraries; rate-limit repr injection to budget per request

edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination: repr index built from same source as generation benchmark
edge_cases.trigger: HumanEval-style tasks based on numpy; numpy repr in training data
edge_cases.risk: eval metrics overestimate generalization; Goodhart on pass@k
edge_cases.mitigation: hold out benchmark library versions from repr index; use separate evaluation set for repr quality

edge_cases.description: Coverage gap for internal or private APIs used in user codebase
edge_cases.trigger: user asks model to call private internal function not in repr index
edge_cases.risk: hallucination guard false-positives on valid private APIs
edge_cases.mitigation: coverage gap policy: explicit uncertainty signal; offer to accept user-provided signature as ephemeral repr entry

edge_cases.description: Docstring distillation loses language-specific encoding such as ReST param vs Google style
edge_cases.trigger: library uses inconsistent docstring style; distiller trained on one style
edge_cases.risk: behavioral constraints silently lost due to format mismatch
edge_cases.mitigation: normalize docstring style before distillation; test distillation recall across multiple docstring formats

edge_cases.description: Repr injection marker conflicts with model natural language in prompt
edge_cases.trigger: injection marker string appears in user task description
edge_cases.mitigation: use unique structured delimiter tokens not likely in prose; test for delimiter collision before deployment

workflow.name: define_repr_schema
workflow.action: Define canonical REPR_SCHEMA: required fields optional fields elision policy; agree on compression notation
workflow.output: schema document and field inclusion spec
workflow.gate: schema reviewed by domain expert and codegen team

workflow.name: set_token_budget
workflow.action: Measure token counts for representative libraries; set per-function and per-library TOKEN_BUDGET; allocate budget across signature type docstring example components
workflow.gate: budget fits target context window at 90 percent or more coverage for benchmark libraries

workflow.name: implement_compression_codecs
workflow.action: Implement SIG_COMPRESS TYPE_AWARE DOCSTR_DISTILL USAGE_EX DEP_GRAPH encoding as per schema; validate round-trip fidelity on held-out set
workflow.output: compression codecs and codec test suite
workflow.gate: round-trip fidelity 95 percent or more on held-out set; token budgets met

workflow.name: run_encoding_pipeline
workflow.action: Execute ENCODE_PIPELINE over target library corpus; produce versioned repr index with VERSION_MGMT tagging
workflow.gate: index passes consistency checks; all entries have schema version tag

workflow.name: build_retrieval_index
workflow.action: Build RETRIEVAL_INDEX over repr corpus: BM25 index over compressed signatures embedding index over repr entries; configure QUERY_ENCODE
workflow.gate: recall@10 90 percent or more on held-out query set

workflow.name: implement_context_injection
workflow.action: Implement CONTEXT_INJECT prompt template; test repr injection with representative queries; validate injected repr does not crowd out task context
workflow.output: context injection policy and prompt template
workflow.gate: injection benchmark: 80 percent or more of generated code uses at least one injected API correctly

workflow.name: run_evaluation
workflow.action: Run EVAL_REPR: retrieval recall@k generation pass@k execution correctness round-trip fidelity; compare to no-repr baseline
workflow.gate: execution correctness 70 percent or more pass@1; 10 percent or more improvement over no-repr baseline

workflow.name: implement_hallucination_guard
workflow.action: Implement HALLUC_GUARD: membership test against repr index; configure COVERAGE_GAP fallback policy
workflow.output: grounding check module and coverage gap report
workflow.gate: hallucination detection precision 90 percent or more; false positive rate less than 10 percent

workflow.name: optional_fine_tuning
workflow.action: If token injection overhead exceeds 20 percent of context window execute FINETUNE_REPR: build repr-code SFT dataset; fine-tune; evaluate against general coding benchmark
workflow.gate: general coding benchmark within 5 percent of base; repr-native generation 10 percent or more improvement

workflow.name: setup_incremental_update
workflow.action: Configure INCREMENTAL_UPDATE pipeline: delta detection from library releases; automated re-encode of changed symbols; consistency checks; VERSION_MGMT propagation
workflow.gate: incremental update produces identical index to full re-index on patch-release test

workflow.name: monitor_latency_and_coverage
workflow.action: Deploy LATENCY_COST profiling; monitor retrieval latency injection cost; track COVERAGE_GAP rate from user query logs; prioritize index expansion
workflow.output: ops dashboard and coverage expansion backlog
workflow.gate: SLA met 99 percent or more of requests; top-10 coverage gaps addressed within sprint

workflow.name: schema_versioning_and_migration
workflow.action: When REPR_SCHEMA changes: increment schema version; write migration scripts; test with REPR_VERSIONING validation; gate FINETUNE_REPR re-training on schema major version changes
workflow.output: migrated repr index and compatibility matrix
workflow.gate: migration produces valid entries verified by schema validator on 100 percent of migrated entries

dominance_rules.name: schema_first
dominance_rules.rule: REPR_SCHEMA must be finalized before any compression codec is implemented; schema changes after codec implementation trigger codec revision
dominance_rules.rationale: downstream codecs embed schema assumptions; schema drift without codec revision corrupts the index

dominance_rules.name: token_budget_gates_all_compression
dominance_rules.rule: TOKEN_BUDGET allocation table gates all per-component compression decisions; no compression codec may exceed its allocated budget without TOKEN_BUDGET revision
dominance_rules.rationale: without budget enforcement individual codecs optimize locally and collectively overflow the context window

dominance_rules.name: hallucination_guard_required_before_deployment
dominance_rules.rule: HALLUC_GUARD must be implemented and pass acceptance tests before the repr-augmented generation system is deployed to users
dominance_rules.rationale: ungrounded generation is a higher risk than reduced coverage; trust requires explicit hallucination management

dominance_rules.name: evaluation_before_fine_tuning
dominance_rules.rule: EVAL_REPR must produce a baseline evaluation report before FINETUNE_REPR begins; fine-tuning targets must be defined from eval results
dominance_rules.rationale: fine-tuning without a baseline produces uninterpretable results and may optimize for the wrong objective

dominance_rules.name: version_tagging_mandatory
dominance_rules.rule: All repr index entries must carry schema version and library version tags before entering the retrieval index; untagged entries must be rejected
dominance_rules.rationale: untagged entries cause silent cross-version API confusion and schema incompatibility

dominance_rules.name: retrieval_before_injection
dominance_rules.rule: RETRIEVAL_INDEX must be built and validated (recall@10 gate) before CONTEXT_INJECT is implemented; injecting from an unvalidated index propagates retrieval errors to generation
dominance_rules.rationale: injection quality is bounded by retrieval quality

dominance_rules.name: incremental_update_consistency_check_required
dominance_rules.rule: Every INCREMENTAL_UPDATE run must pass consistency checks before the updated index replaces the production index
dominance_rules.rationale: stale entries after removal propagate to hallucination guard blindspots

dominance_rules.name: naturalness_statistics_domain_validated
dominance_rules.rule: NATURALNESS-guided elision policy must be validated on domain-specific code statistics before application; do not apply general naturalness priors to domain-specific library internals without validation
dominance_rules.rationale: naturalness distribution varies significantly across domains; misapplied priors cause over-elision

dominance_rules.name: cross_library_namespace_prefix_mandatory
dominance_rules.rule: CROSS_LIB must enforce namespace prefixes for all multi-library repr entries before multi-library generation tasks are enabled
dominance_rules.rationale: namespace collision is a correctness failure not a quality issue

dominance_rules.name: repr_schema_versioning_gates_fine_tune
dominance_rules.rule: REPR_VERSIONING schema major version change must trigger FINETUNE_REPR re-run before new schema repr index is deployed; minor/patch changes do not require re-training
dominance_rules.rationale: model trained on old schema generates incorrect repr tokens with new schema

anti_rework_rules.name: no_codec_without_schema
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not implement any compression codec before REPR_SCHEMA is finalized; codec assumptions embedded in partial schema will require full rewrite

anti_rework_rules.name: no_retrieval_index_before_codec_validation
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not build the retrieval index before compression codecs pass round-trip fidelity tests; index built on faulty codecs must be fully rebuilt

anti_rework_rules.name: no_fine_tuning_before_schema_stable
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not begin FINETUNE_REPR until REPR_SCHEMA and REPR_VERSIONING are stable; schema changes after SFT require re-generating the entire training dataset and re-training

anti_rework_rules.name: no_multi_library_without_cross_lib_alignment
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not enable multi-library generation tasks before CROSS_LIB alignment is implemented; namespace collision bugs require both index rebuild and prompt template revision

anti_rework_rules.name: no_production_deployment_without_hallucination_guard
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy to production before HALLUC_GUARD is implemented; post-deployment hallucination issues require emergency patching plus reputation repair

anti_rework_rules.name: no_version_management_bypass
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not skip VERSION_MGMT tagging in initial index build; retrofitting version tags onto an untagged index requires full re-encode

anti_rework_rules.name: no_latency_optimization_before_correctness_gate
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not optimize LATENCY_COST before EVAL_REPR correctness gate is passed; optimizing a broken pipeline locks in wrong architecture

anti_rework_rules.name: no_docstring_distillation_without_recall_test
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not deploy DOCSTR_DISTILL without measuring distillation recall on behavioral constraints; silent constraint loss requires index reconstruction

anti_rework_rules.name: no_token_budget_changes_post_codec_without_revalidation
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not change TOKEN_BUDGET allocation without re-validating all codecs; budget shifts can cause previously passing codecs to overflow

anti_rework_rules.name: no_coverage_gap_ignored_in_eval
anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not close EVAL_REPR without measuring coverage gap rate; deploying with high gap rate makes hallucination guard ineffective

iteration_protocol.action: revalidate all codecs for schema compatibility; re-run ENCODE_PIPELINE; rebuild RETRIEVAL_INDEX; gate FINETUNE_REPR re-run on major version change
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: round-trip fidelity 95 percent or more on held-out set after codec revision

iteration_protocol.action: re-optimize compression ratios; re-run SIG_COMPRESS and DOCSTR_DISTILL under new budget; validate coverage not degraded
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: repr fits new token budget at 90 percent or more coverage for benchmark libraries

iteration_protocol.action: diagnose: check repr schema changes embedding drift BM25 index staleness; re-index if needed; re-tune QUERY_ENCODE
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: recall@10 restored to 90 percent or more

iteration_protocol.trigger: hallucination rate increases more than 5 percent from baseline
iteration_protocol.action: audit HALLUC_GUARD coverage; check for coverage gaps causing false negatives; run COVERAGE_GAP analysis; expand index for top missing APIs
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: hallucination rate returns to baseline; coverage gap rate less than 10 percent

iteration_protocol.trigger: FINETUNE_REPR shows more than 5 percent degradation on general coding benchmark
iteration_protocol.action: reduce SFT dataset size or add general coding examples to re-balance; re-train with revised mix; re-evaluate
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: general coding benchmark within 5 percent of base model

iteration_protocol.trigger: library major version release with breaking API changes
iteration_protocol.action: trigger INCREMENTAL_UPDATE for changed symbols; update VERSION_MGMT tags; run HALLUC_GUARD acceptance tests; check CROSS_LIB alignment
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: updated index passes consistency check and hallucination guard tests

iteration_protocol.action: profile LATENCY_COST bottlenecks; expand retrieval cache; tune retrieval depth; consider reducing CONTEXT_INJECT repr token limit
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: p99 latency within SLA on load test

iteration_protocol.trigger: coverage gap rate more than 10 percent on user query sample
iteration_protocol.action: run COVERAGE_GAP analysis; prioritize top-N missing APIs; run INCREMENTAL_UPDATE or targeted encoding for missing entries
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: coverage gap rate less than 5 percent on user query sample

iteration_protocol.action: remove contaminated libraries from repr index; rebuild evaluation set excluding overlap; re-run EVAL_REPR; update benchmark policy
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: evaluation set has no overlap with repr index training libraries

iteration_protocol.trigger: cross-library namespace collision detected in generated code
iteration_protocol.action: audit CROSS_LIB alignment; add namespace prefixes for colliding entries; re-run CONTEXT_INJECT validation; update EXPAND_DECODE for new namespace format
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: zero namespace collision in benchmark multi-library tasks

priority_rationale: REPR_SCHEMA first as the structural contract all other components depend on; TOKEN_BUDGET second as the constraint shaping all compression decisions; compression codecs next; NATURALNESS and USAGE_EX are enrichment layers; DEP_GRAPH and ENCODE_PIPELINE build the index; VERSION_MGMT and RETRIEVAL_INDEX make it queryable; QUERY_ENCODE EXPAND_DECODE CONTEXT_INJECT complete the generation path; EVAL_REPR and HALLUC_GUARD gate quality; FINETUNE_REPR is optional optimization; LATENCY_COST COVERAGE_GAP INCREMENTAL_UPDATE CROSS_LIB REPR_VERSIONING are operational and maintenance concerns

validation_protocol.high_risk_node_obligation: nodes with risk_if_wrong>=0.80 must have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
validation_protocol.high_coupling_node_obligation: nodes with cross_topic_coupling>=0.75 must have non-empty revisit_triggers
validation_protocol.conflict_edge_obligation: conflict edges must have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule
validation_protocol.priority_order_completeness: priority_order must list every node id exactly once
